title: FP1 Roundup: Which Formula 2 stars past and present will be on track in Mexico
excerpt:
This weekend’s Mexico City Grand Prix will see plenty of Formula 2 stars from the past, present as well as the future taking part in Free Practice 1 at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez.

A few will be making their Formula 1 race weekend debut, while others will be building on their previous FP1 experience. Here is a rundown of who you can expect to see out on track…

Firstly, Gabriele Minì will be driving for Alpine in the opening practice session, going behind the wheel of Franco Colapinto’s A526 for the first time on an F1 weekend.

Minì will be joined on track by his rival for the Formula 2 title, Nikola Tsolov, who will also be getting his first experience of driving in an F1 race weekend for Racing Bulls.

Hitech’s Colton Herta will be back in the car for Cadillac for his fifth FP1 outing of the season, replacing Valtteri Bottas.

2025 Formula 2 champion Leonardo Fornaroli is also back in an F1 car again for McLaren, having also driven at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya and Spielberg.

Fornaroli will be joined on track by Luke Browning, who will be jumping in the cockpit of Alex Albon’s FW48 for the 60-minute session.

Elsewhere, the Audi Formula 1 Team had previously announced that Freddie Slater – who is set to drive for Invicta Racing in 2027 – will be making his FP1 debut with the team, replacing 2024 F2 champion Gabriel Bortoleto.

Red Bull Racing have also confirmed that Ayumu Iwasa will be taking the place of Max Verstappen, while Frederik Vesti replaces George Russell at Mercedes.

Finally at Aston Martin, Jak Crawford will get his fourth FP1 appearance of the season when he goes behind the wheel of Lance Stroll’s AMR26.

title: Nikola Tsolov to drive for Racing Bulls in FP1 at Mexico City Grand Prix
excerpt:
Nikola Tsolov will make his Formula 1 race weekend debut when he drives for Racing Bulls in Free Practice 1 at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Tsolov has had an impressive 2026 Formula 2 season, and is currently second in the Standings with six victories and nine podiums in total with two rounds to go.

The Bulgarian drivers strong form will now be rewarded with a runout in the opening practice session at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez.

Tsolov, who completed his first test for the team in Imola back in August, is set to replace Liam Lawson for the 60-minute outing.

At the announcement, the 19-year-old expressed his excitement at the chance to make his debut on an F1 race weekend.

“A big thank you to VCARB for giving me this opportunity in Mexico,” said Tsolov. “Following my test with the team at Imola in August, I’m excited to take this next step, build on that experience and learn more about the car and the current regulations. I’ll focus on making the most of the session, working closely with the team and providing useful feedback.”

VCARB Team Principal Alan Permane also added: Running Nikola in FP1 is an important step in his development within the Red Bull Junior Programme. It reflects our commitment to nurturing emerging talent and giving our junior drivers valuable track time and the support they need to learn and develop. Having already worked with Nikola at Imola, we’re looking forward to seeing him build on that experience in Mexico and to the feedback he can provide to help support our preparations for the weekend.”

title: Eleven teams selected for the 2027-2029 FIA Formula 2 seasons
excerpt:
The FIA Formula 2 Championship promoters are pleased to announce the eleven teams selected to compete in the 2027–2029 seasons. Ten teams from the 2026 grid have been retained for the next three-year cycle, with newcomers LN4 Fusion completing the line-up.

The selected teams, listed in alphabetical order, are ART Grand Prix, Campos Racing, DAMS, Hitech, Invicta Racing, LN4 Fusion, MP Motorsport, PREMA Racing, Rodin Motorsport, TRIDENT and Van Amersfoort Racing.

Each team will continue to enter two cars, maintaining a 22-car grid.

FIA Formula 2 CEO Bruno Michel said :“We received strong interest from teams around the world for this new three-year cycle, underlining the strength and appeal of our Championship. We have retained ten of our current teams, who have consistently demonstrated their commitment to providing the best possible environment for young drivers to prepare for Formula 1.

“I am also pleased to welcome LN4 Fusion to the grid. They will bring considerable expertise, and I am confident they will make a valuable contribution to the Championship.”

title: Gabriele Minì set to drive for Alpine in FP1 at the Mexico City Grand Prix
excerpt:
Alpine Formula 1 Team have confirmed that Gabriele Minì will drive for the team in the opening practice session of this weekend’s Mexico City Grand Prix.

Minì, who has been a member of the Alpine Academy since 2023 will get his first run out on an F1 race weekend, jumping into the cockpit of Franco Colapinto’s A526 for Free Practice 1.

The Italian driver gets this opportunity off the back of a strong campaign in Formula 2, where he is currently fourth in the Standings with two rounds to go, having achieved two victories and an additional seven podiums.

Minì, who has previously taken part in the Testing of Previous Cars Programme (TPC) with Alpine this year, is excited to now get a chance to debut on a Formula 1 race weekend.

“I’m looking forward to getting behind the wheel of the A526 and taking part in my first ever Free Practice 1 in Formula One,” said Minì. “Having been part of the Alpine Academy for several years and progressing through the junior ranks, competing in an official Formula One session is going to be a really special moment for me.

“Thank you to Flavio, Steve and everyone at the team for their trust and for the opportunity. I’ve been doing a lot of preparation back at base in Enstone, spending time on the simulator and working closely with the engineers to make sure I’m as ready as possible and able to put my best foot forward both personally and for the team. My goal is to do the best possible job on track and help provide valuable data and feedback to the team to hopefully set-up a successful weekend, where both Pierre and Franco aim to score points by the end of it.”

title: ‘We couldn’t wait for this moment’ – Julianne Cerasoli on the excitement around Rafael Câmara’s F1 promotion
excerpt:
Rafael Câmara’s 2027 plans have been announced with the current Invicta Racing driver set to graduate to Formula 1 next year with the Haas Formula 1 Team.

As someone who has covered Câmara’s career since the very start, Brazilian F1 Journalist Julianne Cerasoli recently sat down with us to discuss his rise to the top tier, and also what this means to her and the whole of Brazil.

“We couldn't wait for this moment,” she said. “We've been following his career since karting and he's one of those drivers that we always heard one day he's going to Formula 1.

“They always said that it's impossible that he doesn't because he's so talented. So the wait is over and everybody's hugely excited about him.

“He's always been quick, but there were a lot of obstacles along the way, because his personality is a bit shy. So he had to move to Europe and go through all the stuff that the Brazilian drivers have to go through that maybe the Europeans do not.

“I think maybe that slowed down his career a little bit. So there were a few years of unknowns when he had to face Kimi Antonelli and he wasn't as strong against Kimi and then his path was a bit slowed down.

Câmara will make the step up to F1 next year with Haas

“So there was a lot of pressure on him in the last three years. But he had to win FREC, he had to win F3 and then he had to try to win F2 in his first shot. So the fact that he has managed to pull it off, it's really, really impressive and it just shows his resilience.”

Câmara’s announcement came just a few weeks after he took the lead of the Formula 2 Drivers’ Championship in Baku – helped by a victory in Feature Race 2.

Looking at his season in total, Cerasoli explains how Câmara’s 2026 campaign perfectly sums up his time in single seaters.

Flight, fishing, travel and classic tunes: Behind the Visor with Emerson Fittipaldi

10 SEASONS OF FORMULA 2: Charles Leclerc on being the first ever champion and being prepared for F1

“I think it's the same as his career,” she said on his season so far. “He started as one of the favourites and then some things didn't go as he was planning.

“That race in Monaco, that's going to hurt him forever, and some things were not really clicking, but he kept his head down and he kept on working.

“He was always saying, ‘I'm just going to focus on what I can control’. He has been working on it and he has been growing in the championship. That race in Belgium, that was absolutely fantastic.

Cerasoli looked back on Câmara's victory in Spa as a drive of a champion

“That was the race of a champion and he is on the up, on the rise at the right moment in the championship. I feel he can do it.”

Câmara is set to be the second Brazilian in the last three years to graduate from Formula 2 to F1, following Gabriel Bortoleto’s rise in 2024.

Cerasoli believes a huge part of the renaissance of motorsport in the country actually started with Felipe Drugovich’s F2 title in 2022.

“It's amazing because not long ago, we didn't have any drivers in F1,” she said on having Bortoleto and Câmara in F1. “10 years ago they were saying that F1 is not going to be on free-to-air TV anymore, that there would be no race at Interlagos, and that Formula 1 would die in Brazil.

“Then it all started with Felipe winning the championship. I think the Brazilian drivers started to understand the changes that motorsport had gone through.

“They understood, ‘Okay, I need backing from a very early age’. I need to leave Brazil and do karting in Europe from a very, very early age. Now we're seeing the fruits of this work because all these drivers that won those championships, they arrived in these championships really well prepared, well backed with their careers in a very good place.

Câmara is set to join 2024 F2 champion and fellow Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto on the F1 grid next year

“They were able to show their talents. We are immensely proud and also hopeful for the future. I think what we're starting to see it in surfing, we have a lot of Brazilian world champions.

“That started, I'm not going to say out of the blue, but it all came together and it became known as the Brazilian storm. Now we are having the Brazilian storm in motor racing as well.”

Freddie Slater confirmed for FP1 sessions with Audi in Mexico City and Sao Paulo

Colton Herta: My Ultimate Driver

On whether Formula 2 and Formula 3 have also rapidly grown in recent years, she responded: “Yes, it's grown immensely. The resilience of the drivers moving to Europe, with everything they have to go through is also the resilience of the fans.

“They have to wake up at 5am to watch the Brazilian drivers, and they love doing so, especially young people who can relate to them. They say ‘They're my age and they're doing wonderful things’.

“I think everybody will be watching F3 for Pedro Clerot mainly, but also all the drivers that are going to be in F2, F3, and maybe we will have another champion.

Cerasoli believes Câmara is a different person once the helmet goes on

“Pedro used to race with them, with Gabi and mainly with Rafa, and they're very good friends. This trio, they work with the same coach, so it's like the same breed.”

When asked what Formula 1 fans should know about Câmara ahead of the 2027 season, Cerasoli says they might be taken aback by him and his talent.

“Well, with Rafa, he's got this soft way of speaking and you don't think he's aggressive, but he is,” she said. “When he puts the helmet on, it's almost as if he's a different person.

“He's so calm and collected, but at the same time, so, so quick. I think you're going to be surprised by him.”

title: Flight, fishing, travel and classic tunes: Behind the Visor with Emerson Fittipaldi
excerpt:
During breaks in the season, it’s crucial for the drivers to reset and make the most of their time outside the car.

We caught up with Emerson Fittipaldi earlier this year to get insight into what the AIX Racing driver gets up to in his spare time.

From getting out on the ocean to getting into a different cockpit, here is how the Brazilian unwinds during his free time.

“Outside the racetrack, I do have hobbies I like to do. Not many, because I'm not so good in other sports, only in racing.

“I really like planes, aeroplanes, and my hobby is flying aeroplane simulators and stuff. So I have a whole setup in the house with really nice stuff and that's where I switch off from racing when I give it a day or two, switch off from racing, reset my mind. So I'll probably do that.

“That passion comes from my dad. And my dad has basically the same passion as me with the fighter jet stuff. And even himself flies the simulator sometimes when he's at home.

“You're by yourself in your fighter jet. You have to go as fast as you can and execute the mission as precise as possible. It's very similar to racing.

“Also fishing. But I only fish in the US, because I like fishing in the ocean. Ever since I moved to Miami, it's pretty common here to go fishing.

So I got used to that and I always liked it. All the time I come back to Miami, I fish here. I don't fish anywhere else in the world. It brings me back all my memories. And I like it just to keep it special for Miami.

“I don’t have that much other things that I do to switch off. I really like to listen to music. Music is a big part of my life, so I really like that. I take it very seriously.

But that's more a necessity for me than a hobby. I like old 80s music, the good stuff. All the top artists from the 80s, Motown, anything. Anything is fine from the 80s.

Freddie Slater confirmed for FP1 sessions with Audi in Mexico City and Sao Paulo

10 SEASONS OF FORMULA 2: Charles Leclerc on being the first ever champion and being prepared for F1

“I travelled a lot already in my life. So every time I go to some tracks, if it’s a country I don't know, like Australia earlier this year, of course, I spend a little bit of days before the race to explore the country.

“I think it's a good opportunity to learn about the country you're racing in. I mean you're already there, might as well just arrive a couple days earlier, experience the culture and everything about the country. That is very interesting for me.”

title: 10 SEASONS OF FORMULA 2: Charles Leclerc on being the first ever champion and being prepared for F1
excerpt:
As we continue to celebrate 10 seasons of Formula 2, we are talking to some of our alumni to look back on their time in the championship.

Today is 2017 champion, Charles Leclerc’s turn to talk about his time in the second tier, as he reflects on his favourite victory, off-track memory and much more.

HOW DID F2 PREPARE YOU FOR YOUR MOVE UP TO F1?

"Formula 2 prepared me in many ways. It was the first time in my career that I had pit stops, and you start thinking about strategy much more than before. Previously, the strategy was quite fixed, but this was probably the first time in my career that I really started to think about that aspect of racing, which is super interesting.

"On top of that, it’s the car that is the closest in terms of performance to a Formula 1 car, so you get to understand more about how aerodynamics affect degradation, the car, and everything around it."

WHAT IS YOUR ADVICE TO THE NEXT GENERATION OF F2 DRIVERS LOOKING TO MAKE IT TO F1?

"My advice is simple: just work hard. Work hard, go step by step, and push flat out."

WHAT IS YOUR FAVOURITE WIN, MOMENT AND OVERTAKE FROM YOUR TIME IN F2?

"Probably Abu Dhabi, in my last race in Formula 2. It was pretty special. The fight with Alex was very tight until the very last lap, and that is my favourite winning moment in Formula 2. That race also included my favourite overtake.

Freddie Slater confirmed for FP1 sessions with Audi in Mexico City and Sao Paulo

Colton Herta: My Ultimate Driver

WHAT IS YOUR FAVOURITE OFF-TRACK MEMORY FROM YOUR TIME IN F2?

"I have quite a few great memories. I was teammates with Antonio Fuoco, who became a very close friend of mine, and I have so many memories from that first year with PREMA. It was a very special team and we all got on super well together."

HOW SPECIAL IS IT TO BE KNOWN AS THE FIRST EVER FIA FORMULA 2 CHAMPION?

"It feels very cool. I remember growing up, I always heard those engines from Formula 2 and always dreamt of being part of that championship.

"It only became Formula 2 once I arrived there, and it was incredible to be able to win that championship. It’s very special to be known as the first ever FIA Formula 2 Champion."

title: Freddie Slater confirmed for FP1 sessions with Audi in Mexico City and Sao Paulo
excerpt:
The Audi Formula 1 Team have announced that Freddie Slater will drive for the team in the first Free Practice sessions at the Mexico City and Sao Paulo Grands Prix.

Slater is set to step up to Formula 2 next year with Invicta Racing after a stellar 2026 season in FIA Formula 3 – where he finished second in the Drivers’ Championship with one victory and eight podiums in total.

The 18-year-old, who was the first driver to be signed to the Audi Driver Development Programme earlier this year, will make his F1 race weekend debut with the team in Mexico, before returning to the track a week later in Brazil.

Speaking at the announcement, Slater expressed his gratitude for the opportunity he has been given.

“Getting behind the wheel of a Formula One car at a Grand Prix weekend is a big moment for me and something I’ve been dreaming of since I was a kid,” said Slater. “I’ve learned a lot this year, and these Free Practice outings with Audi Revolut F1 Team will be another opportunity to keep gaining on-track experience.

“Being part of the Audi Driver Development Programme has already given me some incredible opportunities, and I am grateful for their trust and support. I’m really looking forward to getting out on track: m y focus will be on doing the best job I can, helping the team with its programme and taking as many learnings as possible from both sessions.”

Racing Director and Director of the Audi Development Programme, Allan McNish added: “We have seen Freddie making great progress throughout recent years, both on and off the track; it is the right time for Freddie to step-up. These appearances in Mexico and Brazil will give him valuable experience of a Formula One race weekend, and another chance to continue his development before he steps up to Formula 2 next season. We are looking forward to seeing him in the R26 and supporting him through these two important FP1 sessions.”

title: Colton Herta: My Ultimate Driver
excerpt:
Hitech’s Colton Herta recently took on the task of building his ultimate racing driver and it is fair to say there are some motorsport legends on his list.

From Indy500 winners and multiple-time Formula 1 world champions, it is a list that is hard to argue against…

INTELLIGENCE

“I'm going to pick Dario Franchitti for that. He's a very smart guy, from what I've seen.”

DRIVING IN THE WET

“I'd say Max Verstappen. I think a lot of people think of Brazil, even though Lewis was very strong in that race also. But I think he's just very high commitment. He tends to work more in the wet and you get more in the wet to his talent.”

BEST QUALIFIER

“The best qualifier? I would go Prime Will Power.”

Herta feels the wet shows up Max Verstappen's talent even more

CORNERING

“I think there's a thousand ways to interpret that question. At Indy, James Hinchcliffe is one of the smoothest drivers in the world, as far as how well he approaches it with both his pedals and his hands.

“I'll say James for that one, just because of how meticulous he is. He always turns in at a similar point, but he's always very smooth and calculated. He has a very fine art around driving around Indy from what I've seen, so I will go with him.”

Supporting a brilliant foundation through art: Kush Maini on his special Helmet Design

Rafael Câmara set to graduate to Formula 1 with Haas in 2027

TYRE MANAGEMENT

“I don't have a great answer for that one, to be honest. There was a GT race that I did when I was with BMW in the M8. My teammate was Philipp Eng and he was good.

“But if I’ve got to choose somebody in F1, I think, just because of the Pirellis, we will go with Lewis Hamilton. He seems smooth. He had that one race in Monaco where he did like 900 laps on a set of tyres.

BRAVEST/BIGGEST RISKTAKER

Can I choose myself? I'll go for myself on that one.

Herta identified the smooth driving style of James Hinchcliffe

SMOOTHEST

“James Hinchcliffe, there you go.”

BEST OVERTAKER?

“I'm going myself again for that one.”

ANYTHING ELSE TO ADD?

“I think maybe awareness or mindfulness. Somebody who can be super calm, clear and concise inside the car. I'll put my old teammate, Kyle Kirkwood, for that.

“I think he's very good at that. Staying level-headed and always trying to maximise the day. But there's plenty of drivers that are very strong at that too.”

title: Supporting a brilliant foundation through art: Kush Maini on his special Helmet Design
excerpt:
Kush Maini has had a different looking helmet recently, and we recently caught up with the ART Grand Prix driver to find out more about his new look.

The Indian driver spoke about the meaning behind the design, how it came together and why it means so much to him to support the Akanksha Foundation and his people back home.

“It’s a very exciting helmet, with a lot of meaning and story behind it. There’s a foundation in India called the Akanksha Foundation and I'm doing a collaboration with their art project.

“They're a 35 year old non-profit organisation and their core belief is that reimagining education for a child can lift their entire family out of poverty, so to be working with them is amazing, it's always something I've wanted to do.

Maini talked through the design of his new helmet

“The foundation's own framing of why this matters is art gives children from tougher communities a level playing field and a way to tell their stories, be seen and be heard on their own terms and it's something I wanted to incorporate in my helmet.

“With the platform I have, and I'm grateful to have, I want to be showing the real heroes and the real talent out there.

Rafael Câmara set to graduate to Formula 1 with Haas in 2027

Compromise and identifying balance: How I Race with Oliver Goethe

“So I have two girls who have done an art piece. One is Aalifiya, she has made the mandala on the top and it represents a sense of peace and calm and it's something I strive to have in the car as well, so it matches quite well.

“Then the side, as you can see, is Aditi, but that's more of a memory. It's a bit of home and what reminds her of home and that again resonates with me because obviously I left home when I was quite young and everywhere I go I always take home with me in a way.

The Indian driver talked about what it means to wearing this design on his helmet

“So those two beautiful pieces are going to be with me on the helmet and hopefully bring me some luck and they've done a great job.

“I can't wait to go meet the artists when I'm back home but I think it's a beautiful story and a beautiful objective that Akanksha is doing and I'm very proud to be a part of it.

Formula 2 in 2022: A title-winning reunion alongside an epic F1 debut

Nikola Tsolov: 'We can bounce back' as he eyes title fight redemption

“India is a country where a lot of talent gets overlooked because they don't have the opportunity or don't have the platform or the wealth and we have so much talent that doesn't end up getting seen.

“This is one step closer to evening out the playing field and I'm very happy to be able to contribute in a small way to that.”

title: Compromise and identifying balance: How I Race with Oliver Goethe
excerpt:
MP Motorsport’s Oliver Goethe talks all about driving style and adaptation in FIA Formula 2. From identifying strengths and minimising weaknesses to learning how to best utilise the tools at his disposal, Goethe explains how he goes about going fast.

“I think it depends a bit on the track and the conditions. It's important to have a very good front end in order to avoid understeer. Rotation is really important.

“However, especially in the Formula 2 car, when it's really hot, it's very easy to overheat the rears. So, you know, you have to find the right balance of how much oversteer you can have because it's easy to overdo and underdo and that's what's difficult about finding the perfect balance.

“But, in general, I think good rotation is the most important for me. It's all about adapting, conditions change a lot. There's really a thin line when trying to find the perfect balance, as I said. Also, to drive it properly is difficult.

“It's easy to overdo it with the driving. It's about precision and adapting. I think in F2 especially it's very sensitive with the tyres. It's difficult to stay in the perfect working window. It's something you have to learn as a driver in F2.

“As soon as you start to overdrive the car, it's very easy to lose the peak of the tyres and go in a bit of a downward spiral. It's important to not overdo it, but also to not underdo it, because otherwise you're just too slow. It's really about being precise and managing the tyres well.

Rafael Câmara set to graduate to Formula 1 with Haas in 2027

Formula 2 in 2022: A title-winning reunion alongside an epic F1 debut

“In Barcelona for example, you need to manage the tyre on a quali lap, because you need to have the tyre at the end of the lap in the high-speed right-hander. Qualifying is the same sort of picture, just on a smaller scale. Obviously, the race is longer, so you need to manage it for longer.

“But even in qualifying, it's very easy to overheat the rear tyres with how hard everyone is pushing. Not just in Barcelona, I think in general on the softer compounds it's often easy to overheat the tyre. But it's the same for everyone, so it's important to find the right balance for the car, as well as being perfect with the driving.”

title: Formula 2 in 2022: A title-winning reunion alongside an epic F1 debut
excerpt:
As we continue to celebrate 10 seasons of Formula 2, we are also looking back on each year of the championship’s great history.

Today is all about 2022, and how Felipe Drugovich and MP Motorsport came back together to put a dominant title-winning campaign together.

In addition to that, we had a previous champion make his Formula 1 debut in Monza, while Logan Sargeant earned promotion to the next level…

DRUGOVICH’S DOMINANT TWO ROUNDS

The Brazilian driver and MP’s title-winning campaign was built on consistency but it truly started in Barcelona and Monaco.

Drugovich won three out of the four races across both rounds, starting with an impressive win in the Sprint Race at the Spanish venue.

The MP driver would achieve the fabled double on Sunday, making his Soft tyres last longer than his rivals on the first stint, allowing him to come through the field late on with fresher Hards.

Drugovich claimed both wins in Barcelona before winning again in Monte Carlo

Once Drugovich overtook Jack Doohan on Lap 27 of 37, he would drive off into the distance, winning by 5.5s, having started in P10.

But the winning did not stop in Barcelona, it continued at the Principality a week later.

After taking Pole Position for the Feature Race, Drugovich lined up P10 in the Sprint, but suffered a puncture on the opening lap.

Rafael Câmara set to graduate to Formula 1 with Haas in 2027

Nikola Tsolov: 'We can bounce back' as he eyes title fight redemption

Both driver and team opted to try their hand on the Wet tyres with rain hitting the track, but once they decided it was not wet enough, he came back in for slick tyres before later retiring the car.

The next day, Drugovich would claim victory in epic style, having had to hold off title rival Théo Pourchaire for the final few laps.

Those were two massive weekends for Drugovich, who went from trailing Pourchaire by two points at the start of the Barcelona round, to leading by 32. It was a lead he would not relinquish.

Nyck de Vries made his Formula 1 race weekend debut at Monza in 2022

DE VRIES MAKES ICONIC F1 DEBUT

Monza was a massive weekend for Formula 2, as a champion was crowned but across the road in the F1 paddock, an alumni was making memories of his own.

2019 champion Nyck de Vries took the place of four-time world champion Sebastian Vettel at Aston Martin for Free Practice 1 at the Italian Grand Prix.

He was expecting to be on the sidelines for the rest of the weekend, but on Saturday morning, with Alex Albon ruled out with appendicitis, Williams called up De Vries to replace the Thai driver for the rest of the weekend.

De Vries qualified 13th, but with penalties applied he was promoted to P8 on the grid, and he impressed on Sunday to finish in ninth.

He joined Yuki Tsunoda and Zhou Guanyu by becoming the third F2 alumni to score points on their Formula 1 debut – with Oliver Bearman and Andrea Kimi Antonelli having also joined this list.

Sargeant had to secure a good result in Yas Marina to get enough superlicense points in F1

SARGEANT’S SUPERLICENSE POINTS

De Vries would go on to race for AlphaTauri the next season, and he was joined on the grid by Logan Sargeant – who became Alex Albon’s teammate at Williams.

But the American driver had to work for the opportunity, as he was told he needed enough super license points for the chance to race in F1.

'We can't just wait and see': Gabriele Minì on his mindset and the title fight in 2026

Title fight still ‘very open’ says Câmara ahead of final two rounds

For that to happen going to Abu Dhabi, Sargeant had to finish fifth or higher in the championship or sixth without any penalty points.

Sargeant drove with that pressure at the final round, but he handled it well, crossing the line sixth in the Sprint Race, and fifth in the Feature.

That result saw him finish fourth in the Standings, earning him a spot on the Formula 1 grid.

Drugovich celebrated his title victory in the Monza pitlane

TITLE-WINNING MOMENT AND RESPECT BETWEEN RIVALS

After a Feature Race win in Zandvoort, Drugovich had a chance to win the title in Monza with a round to spare.

The MP driver put one hand on the trophy by qualifying in fourth with rival Pourchaire down in P14.

Drugovich sustained suspension damage on the opening lap of the Sprint Race that forced him to retire and he was had to watch on from the pitwall as Pourchaire made his way through the field.

But after running wide at Turn 2, following a battle with Liam Lawson, the French driver dropped down the order from P11.

Pourchaire would finish in P17, meaning that Drugovich and MP would celebrate their title success at the chequered flag.

Gracious in defeat, Pourchaire would go into the MP garage to congratulate each team member. He would only have to wait one more year to be crowned champion.

title: Rafael Câmara set to graduate to Formula 1 with Haas in 2027
excerpt:
The Haas F1 Team has confirmed the signing of Rafael Câmara for the 2027 Formula 1 season.

Câmara is set to step up after a tremendous rookie season in Formula 2, having achieved three victories, five pole position and seven podiums in total, and he leads the Drivers’ Championship with two rounds to go.

The 21-year-old will step up with a strong resume in single seater racing, having also won the 2024 Formula Regional European title, and the 2025 FIA Formula 3 Championship.

Câmara also has previous experience in Formula 1 machinery with Haas, having driven for them at Testing of Previous Cars (TPC) in August, jumping in the cockpit of the VF-25 at Autódromo Internacional do Algarve in Portimao, Portugal.

The Brazilian, who has been a part of the Ferrari Driver Programme since 2022, is now set to race full time in F1 and he spoke of his gratitude at the opportunity he has been given.

“I’m very happy to be joining TGR Haas F1 Team as a Formula 1 driver,” said Câmara. “It’s an important step in my career and I want to thank Gene Haas and Ayao Komatsu for the trust they have placed in me.

“I’m also very grateful to the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy for their support and for everything they have contributed to my development over the years, as well as to my family for always being there throughout this journey. Now my focus is on preparing myself in the best possible way for this new challenge. There will be a lot to learn, and I’m looking forward to working closely with the team, understanding the car and continuing to develop as a driver.”

Haas Team Principal Ayao Komatsu also added: “I’m really excited to sign such a young, amazing talent like Rafael Câmara. “I don’t need to tell everyone about his achievements in the junior formulas, it’s been very impressive, and in his rookie season in Formula 2, the speed he’s shown in some very difficult moments, like qualifying in Monaco and Montreal – that all goes to show the potential Rafa has.

“He showed when we had him drive in our TPC program in Portugal that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car, he showed us more than just raw speed. Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special. We’re all excited about this opportunity and really committed as TGR Haas F1 Team to nurture this talent and provide a place where he can flourish. We want to create an environment where he’s comfortable and supported, where he can really excel in his capabilities.”

Gene Haas, the Owner of Haas F1 Team also expressed his delight at Câmara joining the team for the 2027 season.

“I’m excited to see what Rafael Câmara can achieve in Formula 1 having seen his accomplishments coming up through the ranks in Formula 3 and now Formula 2 this year. It’s a different challenge at this level but what we’ve experienced through Ollie Bearman following a similar trajectory and association with the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy, these younger drivers are well prepared, and they can make an immediate impact on a team.

“Rafa impressed the team with his TPC performance, so we look forward to building on that and growing our relationship full-time next season.”

title: Nikola Tsolov: 'We can bounce back' as he eyes title fight redemption
excerpt:
While he lost the lead of the Drivers' Championship in Baku, Nikola Tsolov remains steadfast in his belief that there is another twist in the title race yet to come.

The Campos Racing driver led the field for much of the season after a stellar middle phase of the campaign that included three consecutive victories leaving him with six in total.

Though rival Rafael Câmara took over the points lead at the end of Round 12, the Bulgarian says it changes nothing in terms of his approach, and the focus remains on himself rather than responding to others.

"I will focus on myself and on bouncing back from a couple of weekends that I've had some mistakes in," he said. "There have been tough moments that I managed to learn a lot from, so this is something positive I can take on and apply now.

"I've had a lot of ups and downs, just like everyone else, and it's about how you stand back on your feet, and for me, that's what I'm going to be focusing on."

The Red Bull Junior Team driver's form in the middle third of the campaign was devastating, and he says that afforded himself and Campos the room to take tough results and remain in serious contention.

The Bulgarian fought back to finish on the podium in Baku despite a difficult Qualifying

However, he's eager to arrest the slide in performances, and his fightback in Baku on Sunday was evidence he has far from given up on things.

In fact, the Bulgarian driver says he expects the form table to swing back his way if he and the team continue working hard ahead of the final two rounds of the season.

"I think that middle part of the season has really helped me have an easier time with the last couple of rounds and still come out close to the lead even after these things that have happened.

"But it's not the time to relax, and I think that we're looking to bounce back to what we had in the middle of the year. Having had that cushion has been good. Unfortunately, we've lost that advantage we had over everyone else. But we've done it before, I'm sure we can do it again now."

Title fight still ‘very open’ says Câmara ahead of final two rounds

'We can't just wait and see': Gabriele Minì on his mindset and the title fight in 2026

Overall, Tsolov believes that his approach will be rewarded. A focus inward and taking the difficult results and off days in his stride is 'part of the process'.

In Lusail and Yas Marina, it will be about minimising the mistakes and maximising the final opportunities in what has been a gripping 2026 title fight.

"It's very important to stay calm because this is just part of the journey. You can't only have good days. And to have good days, you must have bad ones, right? So I think I'm trying to enjoy the process, as hard as it can be.

"The process is having those mistakes and bad days and unlucky situations, then embracing it, take the most out of it and get back to work and see how you can build on that.

"I've had really bad weekends such as Canada or Miami and yet, we came back and we pulled that margin. So for me, there's always the light at the end of the tunnel. And I think that should be coming soon."

title: 'We can't just wait and see': Gabriele Minì on his mindset and the title fight in 2026
excerpt:
After Round 12 in Baku, Gabriele Minì admits he's facing an uphill battle in his pursuit of winning the 2026 FIA Formula 2 Drivers' Championship.

The MP Motorsport driver is fourth in the Standings ahead of the final two rounds of the season, 43 points adrift of leader Rafael Câmara.

However, at this stage of the year, the Italian says there's not much left to do other than go flat out in pursuit of big results and hope his rivals hit trouble.

"Well, I think the only thing we've got to do is try to do the best as possible," Minì assessed. "So ideally, we'll just try and be in the top three, try and be as far up the order as we can be.

"Then of course, the deficit is - in the end, the thing is that it doesn't only depend on us at this point. I have confidence that we can do better, and we can do well. But then what the others do is not in our control. So, we just have to do what we can do, as well as possible."

With a sizeable gap to make up in the Standings, the Alpine Academy talent says it's all about maximising every single opportunity from here on out.

The MP driver hopes to go aggressive in the final rounds with less to lose than his title rivals

He adds that he will have to make some himself with less to lose than his title rivals. He hopes that will come into play in Lusail and Yas Marina in order to pull off what would be a superb fightback.

"Of course, being at the front is really key. Starting from the front just makes everything easier. So it's a big focus. It would be nice to be defending the lead. It means that we would have more points than the others.

Title fight still ‘very open’ says Câmara ahead of final two rounds

"But we are not in that position. The only thing we can do is to try and chase and try to gain as much as we can before the end of the championship.

"At the same time, it's a better situation to manage. It's a lot about attacking and trying to catch the leaders. We cannot stay where we are and just wait. I did seven or eight overtakes just myself in Madrid and in the whole race, I think there were maybe only two more. So, we have to try and do the same again."

title: Title fight still ‘very open’ says Câmara ahead of final two rounds
excerpt:
Rafael Câmara still believes there is plenty to play for at the final two rounds after taking the championship lead in Baku

Rafael Câmara took over at the top of the Drivers’ Championship in Baku, but with two rounds the go, he knows the battle is still very much on.

The Invicta Racing driver’s strong weekend in Azerbaijan saw him overturn a seven-point deficit to Nikola Tsolov to now lead his rival by the same margin after his victory in Feature Race 2.

It continues a strong season for Câmara, who has three victories, five pole positions and seven podiums in total, and last month he reflected on his campaign to date.

“I feel good,” said Câmara. “It has been quite a good season so far. We have always been in the fight, always strong, and always in a position to fight every weekend.

“I’ve been quite confident, just doing better every day, and we really just try to maximise what we can, focus on ourselves and then be prepared for these two rounds.

The Brazilian driver has won three times this season including last time out in Baku

“I think for the championship, it’s about taking what we can and grabbing the most points available every weekend. We've been doing that quite well in the past rounds, and we were able to reduce quite a big gap to Nikola.

“So now it's basically who finishes ahead is probably going to come out in front. But in the same way, knowing that doesn’t change the approach, it is still the same one. That's trying to keep doing what we have been doing and maximise what we can.”

Laurens van Hoepen moves to MP Motorsport for the 2027 season

Points in Baku debut weekend ‘more than we expected’ says Yamakoshi

Câmara also spoke his mindset while in the middle of the title fight, having had to chase down Tsolov for much of the season.

“To be honest there's some different scenarios every weekend,” he said. “But in the end, it’s to just keep doing what we've been doing.

“I think the focus is really on what we can maximise, and also to prepare the best ways we can, because for sure the preparation helps you a lot after to be confident and to be calm when it matters.

Câmara talked about his mindset going up against Tsolov and Dunne for the title

“We know F2 is a very high level competition, so we need to make sure that we're always doing our best performances, so we can have a good chance every weekend.”

Câmara and Tsolov are the top two, but the Brazilian is aware of Alexander Dunne is 18 points behind him in third, although Gabriele Minì slipped further back after Baku, but still has an outside chance.

Brando Badoer steps up with Rodin Motorsport for the 2027 season

FIA Formula 2 Championship announce 2027 season calendar

Speaking about his rivals, Câmara says the quality of his opponents means he is not taking anything for granted going to Lusail and Yas Marina.

“For sure it's still very open,” he continued. “For sure they are close, but it’s easier knowing that I need to have a bad weekend for them to come up, but also, we know everything can happen in racing.

“You can never, until it's finished, relax. So I just keep focusing on myself and always do our best. So we need to make sure that we're always gaining points.”

title: Laurens van Hoepen moves to MP Motorsport for the 2027 season
excerpt:
MP Motorsport have confirmed the signing of Laurens van Hoepen for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season.

The 21-year-old is currently in the midst of his rookie campaign in F2 and has so far achieved a pole position as well as five podiums and is currently 10th in the Standings with two rounds to go.

Prior to this year, Van Hoepen spent two seasons in Formula 3 and scored five podiums during that time.

The Dutch driver will now join forces with Dutch outfit in 2027, and at the announcement, he revealed his delight at getting the chance to race for his home team.

“It’s good to finally join forces with a team that has been on my doorstep since my karting days,” said Van Hoepen. “I have witnessed their incredible success first-hand, especially in my last five seasons in FRECA and FIA F3, and with the experience of a season of Formula 2 under my belt, I’m confident that I can add more prizes to their impressive trophy cabinet.

“MP is a team of many nationalities now, but it still feels like a natural move to join the home team and race in the orange home colours.”

MP Motorsport Team Principal Sander Dorsman also added: “I’m incredibly pleased that Laurens has become a member of our MP family. A Dutch driver with a Dutch team is always going to be special, and with Laurens’ obvious talent and the debut season that he’s had, it was a matter of time before we put two and two together. With Laurens on board as the first of our F2 drivers, we are aiming to continue our frontrunning F2 form in 2027.”

title: Points in Baku debut weekend ‘more than we expected’ says Yamakoshi
excerpt:
Hiyu Yamakoshi made his FIA Formula 2 debut in Baku last time out, and afterwards he reflected on his weekend with Van Amersfoort Racing.

The Japanese driver qualified 18th and after taking the chequered flag in P17 in the Sprint returned on Friday afternoon to score his first point in P9 in Feature Race 1.

Yamakoshi then finished 14th in Feature Race 2, and speaking at the end of it all, he was fairly happy with how things went in Azerbaijan.

“In the end, I just got in the points, which was more than what we expected overall,” said Yamakoshi. “After a difficult qualifying, it was more difficult than I expected but it was my second ever time driving in F2.

“But I’m happy with the weekend. I learned so many things, I made progress on many things, especially for Feature Race 1 with the Supersoft. My best lap was only half a second from down, and actually pretty much same as Martinius, which is like around top five pace.

Yamakoshi reflected on his first weekend in Formula 2 in Baku

“I impressed myself. Today we were struggling a bit with the balance of the car, but still, I think my pace was around top ten. Before the pit stop, I overtook Bilinski as well, so for me overall the weekend was really positive and nice progress overall.”

On a weekend where the drivers had three races, Yamakoshi picked a few things he learned while racing wheel-to-wheel, and he also explained how racing Formula 3 helped him to prepare for the challenge of Baku.

Brando Badoer steps up with Rodin Motorsport for the 2027 season

Noah Stromsted completes Invicta Racing lineup for 2027 season

“I mean, of course, the rest of the drivers have more experience in Formula 2, so I have a bit of a disadvantage,” he said. “But I think F3 has more fights, with the race starts and the slipstream, the tow effect is big.

“So, I learned a lot this year, especially from Monza, and I just used that experience in Baku as well.”

The Japanese driver talked about what he learned in Baku

Yamakoshi continued to pick out a few things he experienced for the first time, such as pistops and strategies.

“The pitstops were the difficult part,” said Yamakoshi. “I still have to learn how to drive on the limit right way, especially with the colder tyre on the out lap, because I lost around 1.5 or two seconds in the out lap, so I have to improve.

“Of course, it's my first time proper pushing on an out lap, so if I have another chance, I can be better. Also, this is a city track, a street track, and the wall is just next to me, if I go over the limit then I’m in the wall which is not the best.

“So, I took a little bit of margin, I didn't take risks, but if I have another chance at a track like Yas Marina or Qatar, I think I can take a bit more risk, so it should be a little bit better.”

title: Brando Badoer steps up with Rodin Motorsport for the 2027 season
excerpt:
Rodin Motorsport have confirmed the signing of Brando Badoer for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season.

Badoer steps up to F2 after a strong 2026 campaign with Rodin in Formula 3, finishing eighth in the Drivers’ Standings. The Italian achieved four podiums this season, including a Feature Race victory in Monte Carlo.

Prior to that, Badoer finished sixth in the 2023 Formula 4 UAE, Italian F4 and Euro 4 Championships.

In 2024, the 20-year-old also finished fifth in the Formula Regional European Championship and fourth in the 2025 Formula Regional Middle East Championship.

Badoer now continues his rise up the single seater ladder with Rodin, and at the announcement, he expressed how excited he was to continue with the team in Formula 2.

“I’m really happy to be announced as a Formula 2 driver for Rodin Motorsport," said Badoer. "I’m grateful to the team for the opportunity and the trust they’ve put in me, and after such a great season together, I’m excited to continue this journey.

"I really feel like Rodin is a family, so I’m looking forward to working with the F2 team, building on what we’ve achieved and creating more great moments together.”

Rodin Motorsport Sporting Director Benn Huntingford added: “I’m delighted to continue our relationship with Brando as he takes the next step into FIA Formula 2 next season. He’s shown great progress throughout his first season with the team, securing a race win at Monaco and multiple podiums along the way, while playing a key role in leading our F3 campaign. His performances have shown what he’s capable of and we’re looking forward to seeing him build on that experience as he continues his career in Formula 2.”

title: Noah Stromsted completes Invicta Racing lineup for 2027 season
excerpt:
Invicta Racing has confirmed that Noah Stromsted will join the team in 2027.

The British outfit is the first team to finalise its plans for next season, with the Dane joining 2026 FIA Formula 3 teammate Freddie Slater at Invicta.

Stromsted makes the step up to F2 after finishing 10th in the FIA F3 Standings this season, earning a victory at the Red Bull Ring.

On his joining Invicta in F2 next year, Stromsted said he was looking forward to working with such a successful team and was eager to get going with preparations for the 2027 campaign.

“I’m really excited to be stepping up to FIA Formula 2 with Invicta Racing next year. I’ve learned a great deal competing in FIA Formula 3 since 2024 and I feel ready to take on the next challenge in my career. Over the past few seasons, Invicta Racing has established itself as the performance benchmark on the F2 grid and I’m looking forward to getting to know everyone in the team. I can’t wait to start preparing for 2027 and I’m excited to see what we can achieve together.”

James Robinson, CEO & Team Principal of Invicta Racing added: “We’re delighted to welcome Noah to Invicta Racing for the 2027 season. FIA Formula 3 is one of the most competitive categories in junior single-seater motorsport and, after following his progress closely, we believe that Noah has all the qualities to be a future champion, so we’re very much looking forward to helping him make the step up to Formula 2. With Noah and Freddie [Slater] working alongside each other, I’m very excited to see what we can achieve.”

title: FIA Formula 2 Championship announce 2027 season calendar
excerpt:
The FIA Formula 2 Championship has announced today its 2027 calendar, featuring 14 rounds across Asia, Oceania, Europe and the American continent, with two new venues joining the schedule and the return of Montreal, after its successful addition to the 2026 season.

The 2027 season will welcome Istanbul and Mexico City to the F2 calendar, with both events taking place in October. Their addition creates a more balanced championship schedule, reducing the previously extended gap ahead of the final two rounds in Lusail and Yas Island.

The 2027 campaign will get underway in Sakhir, Bahrain, in March, alongside Formula 1, before the field heads directly to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, one week later. From there, the Championship will travel to Melbourne, Australia, before going to Montreal, Canada.

The European leg to the season will begin in June at Monaco, home to one of the most prestigious rounds of the year, as well as one of the most challenging circuits on the calendar. The action will then continue in July at Silverstone, Great Britain, and Spielberg, Austria, back-toback before the summer break.

September will provide a thrilling three-round stretch, beginning at Monza, Italy, followed by Madrid, Spain, and concluding at the Baku City Circuit in Azerbaijan.

In October, Formula 2 will visit Istanbul, Türkiye, for its first race weekend at the demanding circuit, which is making its return to the Formula 1 calendar. The Championship will then head to Mexico City, Mexico, for another highly anticipated new addition to the calendar.

The addition of Mexico City to the F2 calendar was confirmed today during a press conference attended by FIA Formula 2 CEO Bruno Michel, Alejandra Frausto, Ministry of Tourism of Mexico City, Formula 1 Gran Premio de la ciudad de Mexico Managing Director Federico Gonzalez Compean and FIA Formula 2 drivers Rafael Villagomez and Noel Leon.

The 2027 season will conclude in December with two consecutive race weekends, first at Lusail, Qatar, before the Championship travels to Yas Island, UAE, for the season finale.

Mohammed Ben Sulayem, FIA President said: ““The 2027 FIA Formula 2 Championship calendar reflects the continued strength and global growth of an important championship at the heart of our driver development pathway. The addition of Istanbul and Mexico City will bring Formula 2 to new audiences and give the next generation of talent the opportunity to compete on an even greater variety of circuits around the world. Alongside the return to Montreal, these additions further strengthen a truly international calendar across four continents. “I look forward to another exciting season and to seeing the stars of the future continue their journey towards the highest levels of our sport.”

Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1 said: “The 2027 FIA Formula 2 calendar will deliver another exciting season of racing across 14 rounds at some of the most iconic and challenging venues in world motorsport, including the addition of Istanbul and Mexico City. Formula 2 continues to play a vital role as the ultimate pathway to Formula 1, giving the most promising young drivers the opportunity to compete on the same stage as the pinnacle of our sport and showcase their talent to fans, teams and partners around the world. Year after year, the Championship delivers outstanding racing and helps develop the next generation of Formula 1 stars. I would like to thank the FIA President and their entire team, Bruno Michel and his team, as well as all our promoters, partners, officials, marshals and volunteers whose dedication and commitment make this Championship possible. I look forward to following another highly competitive season in 2027."

Bruno Michel, FIA Formula 2 CEO said: “I’m very excited to add three new venues in a financially sustainable way, with the return of Montreal following its surprise addition in 2026 and the first appearance of Istanbul and Mexico City. We will be covering freight costs so that the territorial expansion of the calendar does not financially impact our teams. With a calendar spanning four continents and a carefully distributed sequence of Rounds, the 2027 FIA formula 2 Championship will offer teams and drivers a demanding and diverse season, while bringing the category to new audiences and strengthening its position as a global platform for the next generation of Formula 1 talent.”

title: Joshua Duerksen joins Hitech for 2027 F2 season
excerpt:
Hitech has confirmed that Joshua Duerksen will join the team for the 2027 FIA Formula 2 season.

The Paraguayan is the first driver to be confirmed as part of the British team's line-up for next year, joining after three years of experience in the F2 Championship.

He debuted in F2 back in 2024, and since then has secured eight victories in the Championship along with 16 podiums in total.

Ahead of the move to Hitech, the Mercedes Development Driver said that he was very excited to be moving to the team for next season.

“I’m incredibly excited to be joining Hitech for the 2027 Formula 2 season.

“Hitech has shown for many years that it is one of the strongest teams in Formula 2 and I’m very proud to have the opportunity to race with them. I’m looking forward to getting to know everyone, starting the work together and seeing what we can achieve.

“The new car for 2027 gives us another exciting challenge and I’m really motivated to get started. I want to keep developing, keep fighting for wins and the best results possible on all tracks. I’m confident that together we can achieve some great things next season.”

Jan Sumann, Hitech’s F2 Head of Race Engineering added: “We’re very pleased to welcome Joshua to Hitech for 2027. He’s a proven Formula 2 race winner and we’ve seen first-hand from the pit wall the speed and race craft he brings.

“He has continued to develop throughout his time in the championship and has shown that he can deliver results and perform under pressure. He brings valuable experience with him, particularly as we head into 2027 and the challenge of understanding the evolution of the F2 car.

“Joshua is ambitious, motivated and has already achieved a great deal in Formula 2, but it’s clear that he is hungry for more. We’re looking forward to working with him and seeing what we can achieve together next season.”

title: Bruno Michel's Baku Debrief
excerpt:
It was an important weekend in the fight for the 2026 FIA Formula 2 Championship as we had a bumper weekend in Baku with two Qualifying sessions and Feature Races.

FIA Formula 2 CEO Bruno Michel talks about how the organisation of the round came together and gave his thoughts on the action that unfolded on three consequential days in the 2026 title race.

DOUBLING UP IN BAKU

"We wanted to do that because there was only Formula 2 as a support race here, and for the fans and for the promoter, it was good to be able to increase the number of races that we were having. It was easy to organize, too.

"This is a great track that the drivers really love. It's very demanding and it's very spectacular as well, and having three races here was good.

"I think we've shown that this format is working very well when there is enough track time to be able to do that. So, we'll keep it in mind for the future."

THE TITLE BATTLE KEEPS EVERYONE GUESSING

"The whole weekend was very dramatic. Rodin was flying here in terms of performance. It was quite impressive what they did in Qualifying between Dunne and Stenshorne - 1-2, 2-1 - and they've done an absolutely fantastic job.

"Alex was just untouchable in the first Feature Race, and in the Sprint Race, he was very impressive, too. On the other hand, Nikola Tsolov, who arrived in Baku as a leader, had a very difficult day. And he had an even more complicated time after he picked up a grid penalty for the second Feature Race, having then to start from P11.

"Rafael Câmara did better than Tsolov. He scored strong points in the first Feature Race, but he was in an even better form in Feature Race 2.

What we learned in Baku: The title fight hots up but who has the momentum?

TITLE FIGHT ANALYSIS: How Baku showed that the championship fight is far from over

"That third race was everything you want to see in terms of motor racing. When you have three drivers fighting for the championship, fighting on track for the first three places and all of them on the podium… It was fantastic to watch!

"It's a bit too bad for Alex, because a couple of mistakes cost him dearly. But he was there and he was extremely fast. He cut the line first and classified third. His great weekend in Baku means that he’s moved up to third and he’s closed in on the top 2 in the Standings, with two rounds to go.

"Rafael had a very strong race on Saturday, he did what he had to do, and he was handed the win, which takes him to the top of the Championship. In the meantime, Nikola did not give up. Starting from P11, he put his head down. Ultimately, together with his team, they had a good strategy and the VSC and Safety Car timing worked in their favor. In the end, he did a fantastic race to take P2.

“Seeing the three of them finishing within three seconds and seeing the top three of them on the podium is very, very, very exciting. It's a great way to continue this season ahead of the next two events."

THE TEAMS' STANDINGS CLOSES UP

"Campos Racing has been showing what they can do in Formula 3 and now they're up there in Formula 2 and they're leading the Championship with two strong drivers.

"Invicta Racing has been winning in F2 the last two championships so it's no surprise they're up there as well. We know they're good, and we know they're a very solid team.

"As for Rodin Motorsport, what they have achieved this week in Baky is really impressive, with both of their drivers. They’ve had the pace in Qualifying all season long. Now they found the pace during the races, too.

"It's all done in a very competitive but very good spirit as well, which is the way F2 is. The teams are all fighting extremely competitively on the track. But everybody is respectful of the others and same thing for the drivers.

"There's drama on the track but never outside the track and I think that's really what we want to see in this Championship. We're looking forward to being in Qatar and to be in Abu Dhabi for the end of this thriller."

title: What we learned in Baku: The title fight hots up but who has the momentum?
excerpt:
Round 12 has come and gone and we have a new Championship leader, but while Rafael Câmara is the driver everyone is now aiming for, is he the man in form?

That and more in what we learned across the Baku weekend…

THE TITLE FIGHT MOMENTUM ISN’T WITH THE LEADER

If you thought this was a title fight between just two drivers, you’ll want to reconsider. Alexaner Dunne put together arguably his finest round in FIA Formula 2 so far to well and truly stake his claim over the 2026 Drivers’ title.

The Rodin Motorsport driver entered the weekend 38 points adrift of then-points leader, Nikola Tsolov. He leaves Baku 18 back from Rafael Câmara after the Brazilian took over at the top of the leaderboard.

And even after taking 20 points out of the deficit, the Irishman left Baku dejected after feeling he should have been even closer, but for a misjudgment entering the pit lane in Feature Race 2 that netted him a five-second time penalty, demoting him from the top step to third.

Four consecutive podium finishes and a scoring streak going back a further three races proves that he is hitting form at the perfect moment.

The Alpine Academy driver also earned his first pole of the season having been a near constant presence in the top three on a Friday so far this season.

Though Câmara will have left Baku the happiest of the three contenders, it’s no longer just Tsolov who is the major threat to him in the title fight. Dunne means business and if he keeps his Baku form going into Lusail, he’s the driver to keep an eye on.

Dunne and Camara were Feature Race winners in Baku and both look set to fight to the wire for the 2026 crown

CÂMARA BRINGS THE CONSISTENCY

Câmara took the lead of the F2 Drivers’ Standings for the first time in 2026 with his Baku Feature Race 2 victory.

The Brazilian has a seven-point advantage over Tsolov leaving Azerbaijan, and now has three Feature wins this season, one shy of the Bulgarian’s tally so far in 2026.

The P15 result in the Sprint Race was the first non-score in a race the Ferrari Driver Academy talent has finished since all the way back at the start of July in the Silverstone Sprint.

His near constant presence in the scoring positions in the intervening races, minus one DNF in the Monza Sprint, has helped him fight back in the title race.

TITLE FIGHT ANALYSIS: How Baku showed that the championship fight is far from over

Stenshorne pleased with comeback performance in Baku after tough run of results

That consistency has finally rewarded him with the lead of the Championship heading into Round 13 in Lusail.

Tsolov, meanwhile, has comparatively been in a slump in form after his heights of back-to-back wins at Silverstone and a podium in Spa.

His Saturday fightback in the second Baku Feature Race limited what looked likely to be a major points swing, but he will need to start finding the same vein of form as earlier in the season to keep Câmara under pressure now he’s out in front.

RODIN AND DAMS ON THE RISE

Beganovic's Baku form was further demonstration that DAMS has taken a big step forward recently

In the past two rounds, four teams have taken victories: Hitech, Invicta Racing, Rodin Motorsport and DAMS Lucas Oil.

The latter two have improved their championship standing in the process. DAMS now resides fifth in the Teams’ Standings having overtaken ART Grand Prix, while Rodin sits third after climbing ahead of MP Motorsport and is just a single point behind Invicta Racing.

Dino Beganovic has enjoyed a climb up the Drivers’ Championship himself, now sitting in the top five having earned 58 points across the last two rounds.

The Swede’s teammate Roman Bilinski is also on a run of four-consecutive points finishes in his own right. Meanwhile, Rodin’s Martinius Stenshorne earned pole for Feature Race 2 in Baku, secured a podium in the first Feature of the weekend and is on a points run of his own stretching back five races.

Both teams are on the up at a crucial time in the season, and with two rounds to go, both look well-placed to add another victory to their 2026 tallies before the end.

title: Stenshorne pleased with comeback performance in Baku after tough run of results
excerpt:
Martinius Stenshorne was pleased with how his Baku weekend went overall, although he was slightly disappointed not to have converted pole position into a victory in Feature Race 2.

The Rodin Motorsport driver was in brilliant form throughout the three days in Azerbaijan, following up his P2 in Qualifying 1 with pole in Qualifying 2 by 0.445s.

Stenshorne then finished fourth in the Sprint Race, before taking second in Feature Race 1.

However, in the final race of the weekend, the Norwegian dropped to third behind teammate Alexander Dunne and Rafael Câmara during the pitstop phase, before being overtaken by Nikola Tsolov.

Stenshorne took the chequered flag in fourth, and speaking afterwards, he admitted that there were mixed feelings with his results.

“Overall it's been a positive weekend,” said Stenshorne. “I think we were quick in qualifying, quick in practice, and quick in the Sprint and Feature Race. But we missed a bit today, to be honest.

Stenshorne was very happy to be fighting at the front in Baku

“We made some changes that didn't fully work out. We were just lacking a little bit and then that was enough to take us off the podium. Anyway, I think we have to be happy with the weekend.

“A lot of points scored, moved up some positions as well in the championship, so we're pretty pleased.”

When asked why he and Rodin chose to make some changes after a strong performance on Friday, Stenshorne explained that the nature of the track means that they are constantly having to adapt their car.

“The track is evolving all the time,” he explained.” Obviously, the street circuit is not being run at so much, so the track is constantly changing. I think we were really quick in the Sprint Race.

“We lacked maybe a little bit in the Feature Race 1 and then a bit more again now in the second Feature.

The Rodin Motorsport driver shared why he and the team chose to make changes to their car

“There are some things that we could have done better but overall I think we have to be really happy with our weekend. I think qualifying, especially Qualifying 2 was amazing, so really happy about that.”

The Norwegian has been a constant presence in the points in recent rounds – scoring points in six out of the last eight races.

‘It was much more than a win’ says Tsolov after comeback to second in Baku Feature Race 2

But Stenshorne was delighted to be back fighting at the front of the field in Baku, with the results also helping him go from 11th to seventh in the Drivers’ Standings at the end of the weekend.

“Obviously it was good, it was a weekend where we had a lot of running as well,” he continued. “There was a lot of points that we could take and we took a lot, so that was quite positive for the championship side as well.

“But obviously we wanted more starting first today, but anyway it was a good comeback from some difficult rounds.”
